description: ConceptImplications Duquenne-Guigues canonical basis conformance vectors. Both Swift and Rust implementations must produce bit-identical output for each case.
notes: Attribute encoding: FormalAttribute(namespace, key, value) serialised as {ns, key, value}.
Implications are sorted: premise size ascending, then lex premise, then lex conclusion.
isTruncated is true when the maxImplications cap terminated enumeration early.
The D-G canonical basis is minimal: every emitted implication is a genuine pseudo-intent
and no implication is derivable from the others by Armstrong's rules.
ci-001 (empty): empty context yields empty basis.
ci-002 (two-row): Row0:{a}, Row1:{b,c}. D-G basis: {b}->>{c} and {c}->>{b}.
closure({b}) = {b,c} != {b} and no smaller pseudo-intent Q subset {b}.
closure({c}) = {b,c} != {c} and no smaller pseudo-intent Q subset {c}.
ci-003 (cap-truncation): three singletons, maxImplications=2. D-G basis has 3 size-2 implications;
first 2 are emitted (in combination/lex order), isTruncated=true.
ci-004 (global-attribute): Row0:{a,b}, Row1:{b,c}. b is global (closure({})={b}).
D-G basis: {{}->>{b}}. The implications {a}->{b} and {c}->{b} are derivable
from {}->>{b} and are NOT in the D-G canonical basis.

vectors.description: Empty context yields empty basis, not truncated
Two-row context: Row0:{a}, Row1:{b,c}. D-G basis has two implications.
Three singleton rows: maxImplications=2 truncates a 3-element basis
Global attribute context: Row0:{a,b}, Row1:{b,c}. Only {}->>{b} in D-G basis.
